title: DELETE /v1/sessions/:id returns {terminated:true} but never removes the session — GET still returns 200 afterwards
reasoning: Dogfood 2026-09-06 live repro: DELETE known session -> 200 {"terminated":true}, then GET same id -> 200 with full session payload (session persists; only status stays 'cancelled'). Router source (dist/harness.js DELETE handler) calls sessions.has() then harness.onSessionTerminate() then returns terminated:true — sessions.delete(sessionId) is never invoked. The README contract ('Unknown sessions return 404 with a SESSION_NOT_FOUND error' for DELETE) only holds for the FIRST delete of an unknown id; a repeat delete of a known-but-terminated id re-fires onSessionTerminate. Fix: add sessions.delete(sessionId) in the DELETE handler before returning (same pattern as the cancelled-terminal handling in /v1/cancel). title: [P1] Plugin install doc silently nests the fresh copy and freezes a stale one: 'cp -r h3 ~/.hermes/plugins/h3/' into an EXISTING dir -> stale mirror serves 'unrecognized arguments' for verify NAME / route --session, and hermes h3 exits 0 on the failure

title: [P2] sdk-go sync tag namespace: dispatches carry client_payload.protocol_version, the workflow reads client_payload.version (branch is dead) - decide the sync tag scheme

evidence.run_id: sdk-python run 35855671172 (same dispatch batch logged PROTOCOL_VERSION=v1.1.0)

reasoning: Cross-repo wiring gap surfaced while fixing SDKGO-CI-003: producers send client_payload.protocol_version (sdk-python's workflow reads exactly that key and its 09-23 dispatch run logged PROTOCOL_VERSION=v1.1.0), while sdk-go's Determine tag reads client_payload.version - a key no producer sends, so the branch is dead and the sync tag is always the date tag. Foreman recommendation: do NOT simply switch sdk-go to the protocol version. sdk-go is a Go module, so a vX.Y.Z tag is a published module version and `go get @v1.1.0` would resolve to a protocol-sync commit while the SDK's own release line is v0.1.x. Options: (A) keep the date-sync tag as the sync provenance tag and record the protocol version in the release notes only (current behaviour, documented in the workflow); (B) namespace the sync tag as v<protocol>.<n> so it cannot collide with the SDK semver line; (C) drop the dead branch entirely. Owner call; the h3 board's NEVER-DONE audit and the h3 foreman both skip nothing here.

title: [P1] H3Loader reroute is not durable: resolve() reads static config while reroute rewrites _session_routes — a fresh host (or any Hermes restart) mid-outage resolves pinned sessions to the DEAD harness
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24 (h3-dogfood-2026-09-24-22-15-26), local + fresh bunker box. loader.py:253-287 resolve() matches only against config['sessions']; _reroute_sessions (loader.py:376) mutates self._session_routes, which resolve() NEVER reads. Live proof: with harness killed, (a) long-running loader after reroute: route_session-pinned sessions correctly -> native; (b) fresh H3Loader same config (what a restarted Hermes gateway is): resolve('telegram','-100999') -> 'go-echo' (dead) both before and after its own health passes. Also: _harness_healthy boots False even for a LIVE harness (first pass up to 30s), so boot-time health reads lie. Fix direction: resolve() must consult _session_routes (reroute state) FIRST, then config; optionally re-derive reroutes at load; expose a public health getter.
reasoning: Reroute durability is the difference between 'sessions keep flowing' and 'sessions keep flowing until the process restarts' — deploys/crashes/supervisor restarts are routine for a Hermes host. The happy direction works; the durable direction does not.
worker_summary: P1 fixed: resolve() consults session pins first; session_routes_path config persists pins atomically across restart; worker commit 402f00b (shim), one worker per same-file rule; pushed origin/main; judge 89c39a5c PASS; suite 568 passed/6 skipped

title: [P0] H3Loader circuit breaker can NEVER leave OPEN: health loop skips OPEN harnesses and is the ONLY feeder of record_outcome/allow_request (allow_request has ZERO call sites in src/) — half-open probe never fires, one transient outage disables a harness for the life of the host
detail: Dogfood 2026-09-24, measured locally with the documented knobs (window=2, threshold=0.5, cooldown=3.0): breaker CLOSED at boot, OPEN at first failed health pass (+26s after kill), still OPEN at +300s — harness restarted and healthy from +180s, consecutive_failures stuck at 1, zero recovery. Mechanism: loader.py:315-323 health_check_loop() starts with 'if cb.state == OPEN: skip + reroute + continue'; record_outcome is called only inside the health loop (loader.py:333/341/351); allow_request() (loader.py:118) has zero call sites in src/ — the half-open probe can never be granted. Control: WITHOUT the breaker path, healthy=True returned one pass after restart (30s) — the breaker makes recovery strictly worse than none. Fix direction: the health loop must call allow_request() every pass instead of checking state == OPEN (grant -> probe -> record_outcome), or request-path calls must flow through the breaker; add a regression test that kills/restarts a harness through an opened breaker. Repro: /tmp/dogfood-h3-loader/loader_breaker_freeze.py (config + kill/restart timings in docs/dogfood/2026-09-24b-integration.md).
reasoning: P0 because the breaker is the component that makes brain-swap SAFE to enable: a single transient harness outage permanently pins a harness as broken until the Hermes host process restarts. The class is textbook-correct in isolation; the wiring makes the failure state a deadlock. Diagnostics entry E18.
worker_summary: P0 fixed: health loop gates on allow_request(); cooldown expiry triggers half-open probe with outcome feedback; DEGRADED-probe stranding bug also closed; worker commit 402f00b (shim), one worker per same-file rule; pushed origin/main; judge 89c39a5c PASS; suite 568 passed/6 skipped

title: [P1] hermes-h3 pre-update-check BLOCKs on every Hermes version a current user could actually run: bundled versions.yaml tops out at 0.20.0 while installed Hermes is 0.21.1, and even the matrix's 'planned' rows (0.19.0/0.20.0) BLOCK because the shipped shim is 0.1.0 vs required 1.1.0/2.0.0
detail: Live 2026-09-25 with hermes-h3 0.1.0 (source install) against real Hermes v0.21.1. Root cause: data/versions.yaml's own comment says 'version bumps and this matrix move together', but the shim version was never bumped past 0.1.0 while Hermes moved 0.17 -> 0.21, and nothing owns the cadence. reasoning: A user who hits this BLOCK on every real version learns to ignore the tool, which is worse than no tool: the day a real incompatibility ships, the warning has already cried wolf. The BLOCK messages are well-written but the matrix behind them is a year of Hermes releases behind the fleet it runs on.

title: [P2] pre-update-check warns 'H3 config schema v0 will be migrated to v1' but no migration exists anywhere in the codebase - the WARN is permanent and the promise is phantom
detail: Live 2026-09-25: `hermes-h3 pre-update-check 0.17.0` emits '[WARN] config_schema: H3 config schema v0 will be migrated to v1'. upgrade_check.py:354-377 compares cfg.get('_schema', 0) to CURRENT_CONFIG_SCHEMA=1 and emits the WARN, but grep across shim/src shows NOTHING ever writes a _schema key to the config, and no migration/v1-writing code exists (the config writer save_config/_empty_config in cli.py never sets it). Every config, forever, is 'v0' and will 'be migrated' - a WARN condition the user can never clear and a migration that does not exist. Fix direction: either implement the migration (write _schema: 1 on save, no-op migrate on load) or drop the check until one exists; a permanent WARN teaches users to skip the review the command asks for.
reasoning: A warning that fires on 100% of configs is equivalent to no warning - and this one asserts an action ('will be migrated') that nothing performs, which is a false statement to a user about their own files.
